query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: A pack aluminization surface treatment applied to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will form a thin, adherent Al2O3 scale that significantly improves its oxygen resistance at high temperatures without compromising its inherent tensile ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, exhibiting 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
generation.intervention: Pack cementation aluminization process (or equivalent surface aluminum diffusion treatment) to generate a surface aluminide layer.
generation.conditions: The treatment would be applied at a temperature where aluminum diffusion is effective (e.g., 800–1000 °C) in a controlled, low-oxygen environment; subsequent high-temperature exposure testing should be conducted in air at 1000 °C for durations on the order of 100 hours under strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous, nanometer- to micron-scale Al2O3 (alumina) passive film formed on the surface of the alloy.
generation.mechanism: During the aluminization treatment, aluminum diffuses into the alloy surface and reacts with residual oxygen to form a protective Al2O3 scale. This oxide layer has a very low oxygen permeability, thereby mitigating further oxidative degradation under high-temperature conditions without significantly altering the alloy’s underlying microstructure or mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the aluminized alloy will exhibit markedly reduced oxidation (e.g., lower weight gain due to oxide formation) at 1000 °C while retaining similar levels of tensile ductility (8–16% at room temperature) and high-temperature yield strength (within the 163–530 MPa range).
generation.baseline: The untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr shows poor oxygen resistance under high-temperature air exposure, restricting its practical application despite its useful mechanical performance.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects are expected to hold for exposures up to around 100 hours at 1000 °C in air and under mechanical loading conditions typical for high-temperature applications (strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1). Long-term oxidation or cyclic thermal loading and potential coating delamination effects remain uncertain.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal processing parameters for the aluminization (exact temperature, time, aluminum concentration) and the long-term adhesion and stability of the Al2O3 scale under cyclic thermal or mechanical loading conditions require further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr samples: one set receives the pack aluminization treatment under optimized conditions, while the control set remains untreated. Expose both sets to air at 1000 °C for 100 hours under identical strain rate conditions (10−4–10−2 s−1). Post-exposure, evaluate the oxide scale formation (e.g., weight gain measurements, cross-sectional microstructural analysis via SEM/EDS) and conduct tensile tests at room temperature and at 1000 °C to assess retention of ductility and yield strength.
measurements: Thickness and continuity of the Al2O3 scale (via microscopy)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the aluminized samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in oxidation resistance (i.e., no lower weight gain or oxide scale assessment does not show a protective Al2O3 layer) or if there is a measurable degradation in mechanical performance (reduced ductility or yield strength) compared to untreated cast samples under the specified test conditions.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract A novel metal matrix composite based on the NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy (HEA) was designed by the in-situ formation method. The microstructure, phase evolution, and compression mechanical properties at room temperature of the composite are investigated in detail. The results confirmed that the composite was primarily composed of body-centered cubic solid solution with a small amount of titanium carbides and alumina. With the presence of approximately 7.0 vol. % Al 2 O 3 and 32.2 vol. % TiC reinforced particles, the compressive fracture strength of the composite (1542 MPa) was increased by approximately 50% compared with that of the as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA. In consideration of the superior oxidation resistance, the P/M NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy composite could be considered as a promising high temperature structural material. Keywords: high entropy alloys, metal matrix composites, mechanical properties

In this study, bulk samples of a CrMoNbWV high-entropy alloy (HEA) were obtained for the first time by spark plasma sintering (SPS) of mechanically alloyed (MA) powders at 1200 °C, 1300 °C, and 1400 °C. Microstructure evolution, phase formation as well as wear and corrosion behavior were investigated. The MA powders’ phase composition was found to be represented by body-centered-cubic (BCC) solid solution. The solid solution partially decomposed to Laves phases under the sintering, such as Cr 2 Nb and (Fe, Cr)Nb, and NbVO 4 -VO oxides mixture. The temperature increase to 1400 °C led to a grain coarsening of the BCC phase and decreased the Laves phase content accompanied by precipitation at the grain boundaries. The sintered samples showed high hardness and compressive strength (2700–2800 MPa) at room temperature. The wear tests demonstrated excellent results in comparison to conventional wear-resistant composites. The obtained samples also exhibited high corrosion resistance under electrochemical tests in H 2 SO 4 solution. The CrMoNbWV HEA has comparable mechanical and corrosive properties with the WNbMoTaV type HEA, but at the same time has a reduced density: CrMoNbWV—10.55 g/cm
